title: onprem upgrade surge mitigation and customer rollback runbook
creator: Ethan Park
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported failed on-prem operator upgrades during a staggered rollout of operator-2026.03.2. Failure mode: Helm upgrade completes but operator pods enter CrashLoopBackOff when reconciling CRD migrations at scale, causing control-plane flapping and subsequent Helm release state drift. Impact: Several enterprise Private customers experienced brief control-plane outages (10-45 minutes) and required manual intervention to rollback; one customer escalated to SEV and requested an emergency hotfix and a clear rollback runbook. Goal: produce an emergency hotfix release (operator-2026.03.2-hotfix), ship a validated rollback/runbook for customers and partner with Solutions/CS to close escalations within 48 hours.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy operator-2026.03.2 to a VPC cluster with ~150 CRs and multi-namespace workloads
2) Trigger crd migration job via Helm post-upgrade hook
3) Observe operator logs: repeated migrations hitting race on schema-validation causing panics
4) Helm reports release 'failed' or 'pending-upgrade' due to CRs not reconciling, leaving resources in partially-applied state
root_cause_analysis: Underlying cause is a change in the CRD reconciliation path introduced in operator-2026.03.2 that assumes idempotent migration ordering; with large CR counts the migrations overlap and a nil-pointer in the migration controller path is exposed
Helm hooks rely on controller readiness probes which return success prematurely under heavy reconcile load, allowing post-upgrade steps to continue while CRs are still mutating
Operator crash leads to resource finalizers being left in place which blocks subsequent Helm retries and causes config drift between expected and actual cluster state
mitigation_plan: 1) Immediate: publish a 'safe rollback' runbook for affected customers that details how to put operator into read-only mode, remove migration hooks, and perform Helm rollback to operator-2026.02.x

2) Hotfix: patch migration controller to add backpressure + ordering guard and null-checks, increase readiness probe threshold during migrations, and add a reconcile fence to avoid overlapping migrations
3) Deployment: release operator-2026.03.2-hotfix, staged canary across 3 low-risk customers, validate on high-CR-count test clusters, then coordinate mass rollout with CS
4) Backfill: add automated post-upgrade verification job that asserts CR counts and reconciles orphaned finalizers
5) Communication: send templated incident notice to affected customers with rollback instructions, ETA for hotfix, and dedicated SE/Oncall contact
testing_plan: Unit tests for migration ordering and null-protection
Integration test: synthetic cluster with 500 CRs to validate no overlapping migrations
Canary e2e: staged upgrade on customer-like topology (multi-namespace, 3 AZs) with simulated reconcile load
Upgrade verification: automated post-upgrade probe that confirms operator stability for 30 minutes and no pending finalizers
rollout_steps: Cut branch hotfix/operator-2026.03.2-hotfix and open PR with changes and test matrix
Run CI with extended integration tests (migration stress test) and get 2 approvers from infra/serving teams
Deploy hotfix to canary customers (CS-assisted) during low-traffic window
Monitor: 1-minute token-level logs, operator traces, Helm release state, and run post-upgrade verification job
If canary stable for 2 hours and no regressions, schedule wider staged rollout with CS coordination
